NewYorkPage.title: Build your first AI agent with Microsoft Foundry
NewYorkPage.intro: Follow these steps to set up Microsoft Foundry with your Azure for Students account and create your first AI agent.

portal.title: Go to the Azure for Students portal
portal.body: Sign in with your school account to get your free Azure for Students subscription.

search.title: Search for Foundry
search.body: In the Azure portal search bar, type “foundry” and select Microsoft Foundry.

create.title: Create a resource
create.body: Select Create, or Create a resource.

properties.title: Set the properties
properties.body: Choose the Azure for Students subscription and create a resource group, for example “lead”.

name.title: Name your project
name.body: Give your resource and your first project a name.

review.title: Review and create
review.body: Select Review + create. You’ll see “Deployment in progress”; it takes a couple of minutes.

goToPortal.title: Go to the Foundry portal
goToPortal.body: When the deployment is complete, select Go to Foundry portal.

home.title: Explore the Foundry home
home.body: You land on the Foundry home page. Your API key and project endpoint are here; you’ll need them to connect your app.

playground.title: Test in the playground
playground.body: Back on the Foundry home, select Test in playground and try the sample scenario: a purchase in Dallas followed minutes later by a large charge in another country.

ownAgent.title: Create your own agent!
ownAgent.body: Go to Agents and build your own. Paste these instructions into your agent. If Foundry says you don’t have permission, select Assign me the Foundry User role.

NewYorkPage.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text instead.

gate.title: Unlock the instructions
gate.body: Enter your email to see the step-by-step guide.
gate.label: Email
gate.error: Enter a valid email, like name@school.edu.

brief.title: New message from the customer
brief.subject: Subject:
brief.subjectValue: Help us understand our AI usage and costs
brief.p1: Over the last six months, we've significantly expanded our use of generative AI across the organization. AI consumption is now nearly three times what we originally projected and Finance has raised concerns about increasing operating costs.
brief.p2: We're considering introducing usage limits across the company. Before we make that decision, we'd like Microsoft's recommendation. We need to understand what's driving this increase and what you recommend we do next.
